messages.text: hey, i’ve been feeling a bit off since scrolling online last night. not sure why it’s sticking with me so much.

I hear that something from your online time last night is weighing on you today. It is quite common for digital content to impact our emotions, even when we aren’t fully aware of why. Would you feel comfortable sharing what you were looking at or how it made you feel in the moment? We can explore that together at your own pace.
it's probably just me being tired from not sleeping well again. happens a lot.

Poor sleep can certainly amplify emotional sensitivity and make things feel more intense. It sounds frustrating that this pattern of restlessness keeps coming up for you. Have you noticed any specific triggers that tend to disrupt your sleep recently? Exploring those might help us address both the fatigue and the mood.
i know, it’s been a loop. but honestly, last night it was more this one post i read—really intense story about someone losing their sibling. hit a nerve, i guess.

It makes sense that a story about loss could resonate deeply, especially when you are already feeling vulnerable from lack of sleep. When you say it hit a nerve, does that bring up personal memories or fears related to loss? Sometimes seeing others' grief can unlock our own buried feelings. I am here to listen if you want to share more about what came up for you.
yeah... it brought up stuff about losing my dad when i was young. it’s not like i dwell on it, but sometimes it just sneaks up.

It is completely understandable that grief can resurface unexpectedly, even years after the loss. Hearing about someone else's pain often acts as a mirror for our own past experiences. You don't need to dwell on it for the feelings to be valid or significant. I am here to listen if you want to explore that, or we can just sit with it for a moment.

it’s funny how something like that can just… echo, you know? i care a lot about being there for people, maybe because i know what it’s like to lose someone. so when i see others hurting, it lands differently.

That capacity for empathy is a meaningful way you honor your dad’s memory. It makes sense that you feel those stories more deeply because you understand the weight of loss. However, carrying that emotional load can be especially taxing when you are already sleep-deprived. How do you protect your own energy while still being there for others?
wow… i just realized i don’t actually protect my energy. i just sort of absorb everyone else’s. that might be why i feel so drained all the time.

That is a profound realization that likely explains a lot about your exhaustion. Recognizing this pattern is the first step toward changing how you hold space for others without burning out. Prioritizing your own well-being is essential, especially when your own grief is active. Would you be open to exploring small ways to create some boundaries for yourself?
yeah, i’d like to try noticing when i’m doing that—when i’m taking on someone else’s pain like it’s mine. maybe that’s a start.

That is a compassionate and insightful place to begin. Simply observing that shift can help you separate your emotions from theirs. You might try pausing to ask yourself if this feeling truly belongs to you or someone else. How does setting that intention feel for you right now?
it feels… good, actually. like i’m not just stuck with this heaviness. having one small thing to notice helps.

I am really glad to hear that brings you a sense of relief. Noticing that distinction is a powerful step toward reclaiming your emotional space. Take it one moment at a time as you practice this new skill. I am here to support you whenever you need to process these feelings further.
thank you for listening. i feel like i actually said some real things today, and that helped.

You are very welcome for sharing your story. It takes real courage to speak those difficult truths aloud. I hope this sense of relief carries you through the rest of your day. Please know I am here whenever you are ready to talk again.
